clue.text: I say, I say, that's ambiguous!

definitions.text: I say, I say, that's ambiguous!

parts.words: I say, I say, that's ambiguous!
parts.note: the music-hall catchphrase repeats 'I say', so it is speech doubled, while equivocal, evasive speech is also what the phrase names

explanation.surface: A comedian's catchphrase is greeted with a complaint that it means two things.
explanation.definitionFit: Evasive, deliberately unclear speech is called by this name, and saying 'I say' twice is literally talk done twice.

clue.text: Meaning a uniped doctor

parts.note: a uniped has one foot: I (one) and FT (foot)

explanation.surface: Someone asks what a one-legged physician means.
explanation.walkthrough: A uniped is a one-footed creature, so 'a uniped' gives I FT (one foot).
explanation.definitionFit: The gist or general sense of what is said is its meaning.

clue.text: Release articles in French about primitive housing

indicators.note: the French articles go around the word for crude housing

parts.note: un and le are French articles
a shack is a crude hut

explanation.surface: A French news piece reports on crude shelters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' places SHACK between UN and LE.
explanation.definitionFit: To free someone from chains or restraints is to release them.

clue.text: Gentlemen, you may smoke when day is done

definitions.meaning: the after-dinner moment when men are permitted cigars
dusk, when drivers must switch on vehicle lamps

explanation.definitionFit: The smoking sense: when cigars may be lit after the loyal toast; the dusk sense: the legal hour for vehicle lamps.

clue.text: Man in betting ring lost all, reduced to rags

indicators.note: the man's name loses the three letters of the next word

parts.note: Richard Tattersall founded the horse auction house, and Tattersalls is the betting enclosure at racecourses
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gambler at the racecourse loses everything and ends up in rags.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' takes ALL from TATTERSALL; Tattersalls is the main betting enclosure at British racecourses.
explanation.definitionFit: Torn shreds of clothing are rags.

clue.text: Farmers cut loss by destroying- Ins them?

definitions.text: Farmers cut loss by destroying- Ins them?

indicators.note: destroying the phrase smashes its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Farmers limit their losses by killing the pests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroying' rearranges CUT LOSS; '- Ins' is stray OCR noise in the held text.
explanation.definitionFit: Swarming grasshoppers devour crops, so farmers kill them to reduce losses.

clue.text: Crazy, giving this blow in the back

indicators.note: read 'in the back', the word for crazy is taken back to front

parts.note: bats is slang for crazy, as in 'going bats'

explanation.surface: Someone mad delivers a treacherous blow in the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns BATS round to give the answer; the surface leans on 'stab in the back', which helps the definition hide.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrust with a knife is a blow delivered with a blade.

clue.text: Author Anthony's opening and closing metaphor

indicators.note: only the opening and closing stretches of the author's name are kept, the middle dropped

parts.note: Anthony Trollope was the Victorian novelist of Barchester Towers

explanation.surface: A novelist's first and last chapters use a figure of speech.
explanation.walkthrough: Keep TRO and PE, the opening and closing of TROLLOPE, dropping LLO.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure of speech such as a metaphor is a figurative device.

clue.text: Party returned embracing one later sort of pact

indicators.note: the reversed party wraps itself around the other pieces
the party's abbreviation is turned back to front

parts.note: Lab is short for the Labour Party
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A political party comes back to sign a deal later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns LAB into BAL; 'embracing' puts I and LATER inside it: B + ILATER + AL.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-sided agreement between two nations is this kind of treaty.

clue.text: His theft timely, they say — off-putting chap

definitions.meaning: the proverb says putting things off is the thief of time, so this man steals time
a man who puts things off

explanation.definitionFit: The proverb sense: delay is the thief of time; the other: a man who defers tasks.

clue.text: One thing's unravelled by perception

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: something unravelled has had its threads pulled loose, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written with its S, the letters of 'things'

explanation.surface: A single object is understood by being perceived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unravelled' rearranges THINGS to NSIGHT, which follows I for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Perception in the sense of deep understanding is a synonym.

clue.text: Lewis's vehicular instability

parts.note: a vehicle such as a motor car
a ship or vehicle that is unstable will roll from side to side

explanation.surface: Someone called Lewis has a car that wobbles on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'Lewis's' surname: Lewis Carroll wrote Alice in Wonderland.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of Alice's Adventures in Wonderland wrote as Lewis followed by this surname.

clue.text: False female seen in characteristic topless gown

parts.note: a trait is a distinguishing characteristic

indicators.note: topless means the first letter is cut off the word for gown

parts.note: a gown is a dress

explanation.surface: A deceitful woman is spotted in a distinctive dress that leaves her shoulders bare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes the D from DRESS, leaving RESS after TRAIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who betrays her country or cause is false to it, a female traitor.

clue.text: Box forms part of a trunk

definitions.meaning: a large lidded container for storing things
the trunk is the torso, and the upper front of it between neck and belly

explanation.definitionFit: Box: a sturdy storage container; part of a trunk: the front of the human torso holding heart and lungs.

clue.text: Compare right to hold king imprisoned

indicators.note: the king is locked up inside the word for a legal right

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch is jailed after a comparison of rights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imprisoned' puts K inside LIEN; 'to hold' just echoes that container idea in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To compare one thing to another is to draw a likeness between them.

clue.text: Modern lady worried about arranging treat

indicators.note: the scrambled lady goes around the other scrambled word
worried here means tugged about, so these letters are jumbled
arranging puts the letters of treat into a fresh order

explanation.surface: An up-to-date woman frets while preparing a treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' makes L...DAY from LADY; 'arranging' makes ATTER from TREAT, placed inside by 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: Recent or present-day, belonging to current times.

clue.text: He supports the organist going round America

indicators.note: the organist's name encircles the abbreviation for America

parts.note: Sir John Stainer was a celebrated English organist and composer
US is short for the United States of America

explanation.surface: Someone backs the church organist on a tour of America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' puts US inside STAINER: S + US + TAINER.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone who keeps something going or upholds it is a supporter.

clue.text: Food that gives a queer turn to chaps in it

indicators.note: the chaps are put inside the rearranged letters
queer in its old sense of odd, so these letters are turned strange

parts.note: chaps are men

explanation.surface: Something to eat that makes the men who eat it feel odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'queer' rearranges TURN IT to NUTRIT; 'in' puts MEN inside: NUTRI + MEN + T.
explanation.definitionFit: Nourishment is what food provides.

clue.text: Replanning of outer slum very shaky

indicators.note: replanning means laying out again, so the letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: Redevelopment of a run-down suburb is on uncertain ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Replanning of' rearranges OUTER SLUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Trembling or quivering, so very unsteady.

clue.text: Townsman's work on Pindar sadly unfinished

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work

indicators.note: sadly in the sense of badly done, so the letters are jumbled
unfinished means the poet's name loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A man writes a piece on the Greek poet Pindar but sadly never finishes it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' drops R from PINDAR; 'sadly' rearranges PINDA to PIDAN. Pindar was a Greek lyric poet.
explanation.definitionFit: An Eton boy living in town houses rather than college, historically a town dweller.

clue.text: Stout stem

definitions.meaning: to stem a flow is to stop it, as with bleeding

explanation.definitionFit: Stout: loyal and firm; stem: to stop a flow of blood.

clue.text: All you need to start a betting establishment

definitions.text: you need to start a betting establishment
definitions.meaning: the totalizator, or tote, is a betting system whose name begins with these five letters

explanation.definitionFit: All: the complete sum; the betting sense: the totalizator, the tote, has these letters at its start.

clue.text: Crew consumed, some say

indicators.note: signals that the word for consumed is heard, not spelt

parts.note: ate means consumed

explanation.surface: A ship's company has eaten, it is reported.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing crew of eight oarsmen is called by its number.

clue.text: Composer's grand fortune

parts.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand
luck is fortune

explanation.surface: A composer has enormous good fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: Christoph Willibald Gluck was the 18th-century composer of Orfeo ed Euridice.
explanation.definitionFit: Gluck was a German operatic composer famous for Orfeo ed Euridice.

clue.text: A simple little quarrel he takes to court

parts.note: plain means simple
a tiff is a minor quarrel

explanation.surface: A trivial dispute ends with someone suing.
explanation.definitionFit: The party who brings a lawsuit against another is the claimant.

clue.text: Joins the commotion about a point

indicators.note: the commotion goes around the compass point

parts.note: a fuss is a commotion
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone gets into a fuss over a single point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts E inside FUSS.
explanation.definitionFit: To fuse things is to melt them together, joining them.

clue.text: Played part as tattoo artist ?

parts.note: a tattoo is also a drumbeat, so the artist here beats one out on a drum rather than inking skin

explanation.surface: Someone takes on the role of a tattooist.
explanation.definitionFit: Beating a tattoo means rapping out a rhythm on a percussion instrument.

clue.text: Mad Margaret's myristic diet

parts.note: nut, as in 'off one's nut', suggests madness; a nut is a crazy person
Meg is a pet form of Margaret, here with its possessive S

explanation.surface: An eccentric woman eats a peculiar diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'myristic' comes from Myristica, the botanical genus of the spice tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Myristica fragrans is the tree yielding this spice, so seeds of it make a myristic diet.

clue.text: Country bumpkin lacks money for a pair of oxen

indicators.note: the bumpkin is missing a letter standing for money

parts.note: a yokel is a rustic simpleton
L stands for pound (libra), British money

explanation.surface: A rustic too poor to buy two oxen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacks' removes L (pound) from YOKEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Two draught animals harnessed together are called by the name of their harness, as in 'a yoke of oxen'.

clue.text: They live alone if household work includes it

parts.note: an is an archaic word for if

indicators.note: the word for household work takes the other word inside it

parts.note: chores are household tasks

explanation.surface: Hermits are those who do housework with that thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'includes' puts IT inside CHORES after AN, the old word for 'if' ('an it please you').
explanation.definitionFit: Hermits who withdraw from society for religious reasons are solitary dwellers.
